summary: Pascale Hugon works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and taught Flavio A. Geisshuesler.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, working in religious and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger is a Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley, studying under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman. She was Curator at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco and taught at Berkeley.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1975–1997), IAS (1998), and the University of Washington (1997).

Patricia Fister specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After receiving her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas, she taught there (~1983–1990) before serving as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1991–2018).

Sinology and Tibetology scholar Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani completed graduate study at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zumo Zhou, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania supervised by Perry Link.

Patrick Jory is a historian who studied at the University of Western Australia and earned his Ph.D. under Craig J. Reynolds at the Australian National University (~1991–1996). He joined the University of Queensland around 2008.

Patrick McAllister works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Vienna (~2006–2011) under Helmut Krasser, having also studied there under Ernst Steinkellner and Karin Preisendanz.

Patrick Olivelle, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Oxford and Pennsylvania under Richard Gombrich, Thomas Burrow, and Ludo Rocher. He chaired departments at Indiana University (~1984–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (1991).
Patrick Pranke is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman (attested 2004). He has taught Brandon J. Harwood.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at Cornell University. She held posts at Sonoma State University, the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, and California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).
Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1980–1997).

Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hermann Grassmann (~1870–1876). He worked at Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919) and taught Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki.

Paul Copp is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD). He held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Western Michigan University, and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura. He held a post as professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Numrich is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at the University of Michigan (1992). In 2006, he was attested at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.
